item.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco is expected at the end of November. CAS said in a statement that a hearing of the case took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The panel have begun and continue their deliberations,” the organisation which resolves international sports disputes explained. “The CAS arbitrators have decided to issue a complete ruling which includes legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026.” At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred by chaotic scenes near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. item.title: Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed evacuation warnings and move to higher ground following flooding that submerged 18 communities in the Doma Local Government Area, killing two people and displacing several others. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists in Lafia on the impact of the disaster in the affected communities. Aboki said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency to visit the affected communities to assess the damage and determine the necessary interventions. He said the government was working towards providing assistance to residents affected by the disaster. “We are hoping that anytime this week concrete actions will be taken by government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and condole with them,” the commissioner said. According to him, two people have died as a result of the flooding, while several others have been displaced. Buildings and farmlands were also reportedly destroyed. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki said residents had been advised against returning to their homes until the floodwaters receded. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon; it will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. The commissioner said the government was also prepared to provide support and relief supplies to affected residents to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks following the flooding. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered within larger settlements, complicating efforts to assess the full extent of the damage and the number of people affected. Aboki cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly affected, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also said to be experiencing the impact of the flooding. The government urged residents in vulnerable areas to prioritise their safety and remain in safer locations until the floodwaters had sufficiently receded. item.title: 40 years after Dele Giwa’s killing, MRA demands justice
item.description: By Elizabeth Osayande Media Rights Agenda (MRA) has called on the Federal Government to implement a court order directing it to investigate the assassination of renowned journalist and founding Editor-in-Chief of Newswatch magazine, Dele Giwa, and prosecute those found responsible. The call came on Monday, October 19, 2026, as Nigeria marked the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s death. He was killed on October 19, 1986, by a parcel bomb delivered to his residence in Ikeja, Lagos. In a statement issued in Lagos, the media rights organisation described the failure to resolve the case four decades later as a “shameful reminder of the entrenched culture of impunity for attacks against journalists in Nigeria.” MRA’s Deputy Executive Director, Ayode Longe, said the anniversary should go beyond remembering Giwa’s contributions to journalism and should prompt renewed scrutiny of the failure to deliver justice. “Forty years is far too long for the assassination of a journalist of Dele Giwa’s stature to remain unresolved. His killing must not be reduced to a recurring anniversary in Nigeria’s media calendar, accompanied by tributes and expressions of outrage but without meaningful progress towards accountability,” Longe said. He recalled that on February 16, 2024, MRA secured a judgment at the Federal High Court in Abuja in a suit against the Attorney-General of the Federation. According to him, the court ordered the Federal Government to investigate Giwa’s murder and other unresolved killings of journalists, and ensure the prosecution of those responsible. Longe said the government had yet to demonstrate progress or report concrete steps taken to establish the facts surrounding the killings, identify those responsible and pursue accountability in accordance with the law. He described the lack of visible action as a disregard for a valid and subsisting judicial order. The MRA official urged the Attorney-General of the Federation, the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant authorities to provide a clear account of the steps taken to implement the judgment. item.title: Ukraine Received ‘No Early Warning’ Of Russian Strikes — Zelensky
item.description: Ukraine did not receive an early warning from allies about incoming Russian ballistic strikes that targeted energy facilities in the Kyiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday. Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv region and over 200 drones across the war-torn country, Zelensky said. AFP reporters heard air alerts and explosions ringing out in the capital. “Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners,” Zelensky said on social media. Workers clear the rubble from a metro station following a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 19, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Photo by SERGEI SUPINSKY / AFP Last week Kyiv said there had been no warning from the United States of similar strikes, leaving virtually no time for residents to take shelter. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied earlier on Monday that there had been any suspension of intelligence sharing with Ukraine. “There has been no pause,” Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan when asked about Ukraine’s claims, calling on Zelensky to “focus” on ending the war with Russia. Trump, who says he has made a deal with Russia to secure fuel exports in exchange for the easing of sanctions, has made renewed attacks on Zelensky in recent days over the war. The US leader wrote on his Truth Social platform on Sunday that he was making “great progress” in negotiating peace between Russia and Ukraine, but claimed: “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him… he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.” Workers clear the rubble from a metro station following a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 19, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Photo by SERGEI SUPINSKY / AFP But Zelensky, in a post on Monday, hit back at the claims, saying that “Ukraine never wanted this war, and we have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to bring this war to a dignified end”. “Russia’s response, time and again, has been ballistic missiles, ‘shaheds’, and killings,” Zelensky said. “When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine’s air defense are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners,” he added. item.title: UCL: PSG vs Barcelona, Bayern vs Arsenal headline Champions League Matchday 3
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Paris Saint-Germain host Barcelona on Tuesday in the standout clash of Champions League Matchday 3, with Bayern Munich and Arsenal meeting in another heavyweight tie on Wednesday. Barcelona arrive in Paris after winning their opening two matches, while PSG will look to build on their 4-2 victory over Manchester City. The fixture also reunites Barcelona with former coach Luis Enrique, now in charge of the defending champions. Bayern welcome an Arsenal side that has yet to concede in this season’s Champions League. Elsewhere, Aston Villa host Viking, Manchester City face AEK Athens, Liverpool take on Villarreal and Real Madrid meet RB Leipzig. item.title: Kenyan cult leader faces verdict over 191 starvation deaths
item.description: A Mombasa court will deliver a long-awaited verdict on Monday in the trial of a self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher and his associates, accused of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the cult base inland from the Kenyan beach resort of Malindi, in what became known as the “Shakahola Forest Massacre”. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie is alleged to have incited his acolytes to starve to death in order to “meet Jesus”. Mackenzie and his associates pleaded not guilty to 191 counts of murder in 2024. He has also denied charges of manslaughter and terrorism in separate cases. In the three years since the grisly discovery, more bodies of children, women and men have been unearthed, bringing the total to well over 400. Mackenzie looked impassive as he arrived at Mombasa Law Courts on Monday with 29 other accused, who descended from a barred-window bus hand-cuffed in pairs. Relatives of the victims were also in court, many making their way to Mombasa from rural communities along the coast. Francis Wanje, 62, lost eight family members, including his daughter and two grandchildren, in Shakahola. “This day, to me, is a very, very important day,” he told AFP before the session started. “We are expecting a ruling that will be a lesson to the whole public, so that such kinds of things will not happen again,” he said, expressing anger over the initial government inaction. There have been calls in Kenya for tougher regulations on religious organisations after it emerged that Mackenzie had been arrested twice in the past but released. The prosecution alleges that Mackenzie “initiated and directed” extreme fasting at his 800-acre (325 hectare) ranch in Shakahola Forest, claiming there was a “structured hierarchy of death” which said children should die first, followed by teenagers, women, and then men. The children mostly died from starvation, but also from “asphyxia, neck compression and traumatic head injury”, prosecutors said, based on post-mortems and police reports. Mackenzie’s lawyers said the case was “largely founded on circumstantial evidence, hearsay accounts and inconclusive forensic findings”. – Case exposed – Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023, after a rights group tipped off authorities and some followers were rescued. The subsequent police operation exposed hundreds of shallow mass graves, with a soaring death toll that required a pause in excavations as local morgues ran out of space. In January, Mackenzie was charged over a further 52 bodies found at a nearby village. The self-styled pastor has a history of extremism and evaded law enforcement for years. item.title: Semenyo ruled out for eight weeks as Man City sweat over Haaland
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Antoine Semenyo is expected to miss around eight weeks with a knee injury, while Erling Haaland remains a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League match against AEK Athens on Tuesday. According to Sky Sports, City manager Enzo Maresca said scans showed Semenyo’s injury was less severe than the club had feared. The forward was hurt during Saturday’s 3-2 win over Ipswich Town. “Now the most important thing is for him to recover,” Maresca said. “When he is back in December, it will be like a new player.” Haaland also limped off after the Ipswich match, but Maresca said he could still be available for Tuesday’s game. The striker felt better on Monday, though City were waiting to assess him in training. “We have some doubts after Saturday’s game,” Maresca said. “He was quite good yesterday, better, so we’ll see today.” Mateo Kovacic, Nico O’Reilly and Matheus Nunes also had injury concerns during the Ipswich match. Maresca said the other players were “more or less all okay”, with Semenyo the only player expected to be out for an extended period. City have three points from their first two Champions League matches as Maresca said the team would aim to beat AEK with its best available players after losing its previous game to Paris Saint-Germain. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s big picture: Nigeria’s opposition parties are openly disagreeing over a proposed single presidential candidate, while the Federal Government is challenging the World Bank’s assessment of its debt burden. Preparations for state policing are advancing despite unfinished legislation. Across Africa, Congo’s Ebola epidemic has reached an eighth province. Globally, falling oil prices are providing some relief as concerns about AI investment continue to unsettle financial markets. 1. Nigeria 2027: Obi-Kwankwaso Ticket Rejects Calls For A Single Opposition Candidate Obi is a former Anambra State governor What happened : Former Kano State Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has reaffirmed that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential ticket will not withdraw in favour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). In a statement on Sunday, 18 October, Kwankwaso, the NDC vice-presidential candidate, rejected suggestions that Peter Obi might step aside for ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar. He also denied allegations that the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket was working indirectly for the ruling APC. The exchange follows renewed disagreement between the ADC and NDC over opposition cooperation ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Why it matters : The statements establish that discussions about opposition cooperation have not produced an agreement on a joint presidential ticket. Political implications : The disagreement highlights unresolved questions about party coordination, policy differences, and the terms of any possible alliance. It does not establish how voters will respond. What to watch : Further statements from the ADC and NDC, any formally announced agreements, and the parties’ separate campaign programmes. 2. The Bank reported that federal interest payments reached ₦7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026, equivalent to 124 per cent of reported federal revenue. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele argues that the comparison is misleading because the interest figure includes obligations serviced on behalf of states, while the revenue figure excludes certain government income. The ministry acknowledges the underlying figures but emphasises that: Federal revenue increased 72 per cent, from ₦3.6 trillion to ₦6.2 trillion. Interest payments increased 38 per cent, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion. The reported interest-to-revenue ratio declined from 156 per cent to 124 per cent. item.title: Passports: Nigerians in Qatar excited over improved service, honour Yakubu
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Nigerians in Qatar have honoured the Nigerian Ambassador to the country, Prof. Mahmood Yakubu, with an award for improved consular service, following the recent delivery of new passports to hundreds of them in a record time of two weeks. The presentation was made at an elaborate ceremony organised by the Nigerians in Diaspora Organisation NIDO, Qatar chapter, to mark Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary. Hundreds of Nigerians in Qatar recently received their new passports within two weeks, a turnaround the community described as record time. Yakubu used the occasion to commend the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, and the Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nandap for their support. He specifically thanked them for the prompt deployment of the intervention team and the production of the passports. The event was attended by the Executive Director of the Workers Support and Insurance Fund under the Qatari Ministry of Interior, Ms Kholoud Saif Al Kubaisi, and members of the diplomatic community. item.title: Marseille’s official store looted as protests rock France
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Olympique de Marseille’s official store on the city’s La Canebière avenue was looted during weekend unrest, the Ligue 1 club said on Monday. According to Reuters, the incident came as France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, with protests over rising prices and declining public services. Thousands of people were arrested, while shops were looted or damaged. Marseille authorities imposed a ban on public gatherings and demonstrations across the city on Monday following violent protests and looting. The club condemned the attack and said it stood in solidarity with Puma, its partner that operates the store. The damage has forced the shop to close temporarily, though fans can still visit Marseille’s other official stores. Marseille said it would update supporters when conditions allow the La Canebière store to reopen. The club said in a statement: “Olympique de Marseille condemns in the strongest possible terms the acts of violence and looting targeting its official store on the Canebière and expresses its solidarity with its partner Puma, which operates the store. These events have caused significant property damage, forcing the club to temporarily close this store to the public. Fans may, however, continue to visit OM’s other official stores in Marseille. The club will inform its fans as soon as conditions allow for a reopening.” The club sits ninth in Ligue 1 after seven matches. It returns to action on Thursday with an away Europa League game against Austria’s Sturm Graz. The post Marseille’s official store looted as protests rock France appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Former Delta governor Uduaghan dies at 71
item.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire Former Governor of Delta State Emmanuel Uduaghan has died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. A statement signed by his son Toju Anire Uduaghan on behalf of the family said the ex-governor died on Monday. Read Also: Uduaghan is alive, recuperating – Family, aide debunk death rumour “It is with hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow that we announce the passing to glory of our beloved Father, Brother, Uncle, and Patriarch, His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State, who departed this world on the morning of 19th October 2026,” the statement said. “His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria. “He was a source of strength, a father figure, a beloved brother and uncle, and a respected elder. We will deeply miss his presence and forever cherish the memories and legacy he leaves behind. “He served as Commissioner for Health from 1999 to 2003, Secretary to the Delta State Government from 2003 to 2007, and Governor of Delta State from 2007 to 2015. Throughout his years in public service, he demonstrated a commitment to the human and infrastructural development of Delta State.” The statement said Uduaghan’s death was a profound loss to the family, the people of Delta State, and Nigeria at large. “We are grateful to Almighty God for his life, his service, and the legacy he leaves behind. “We pray that Almighty God, in His infinite mercy, will grant his soul eternal rest and comfort our family, friends, associates, former colleagues, and all who mourn this painful loss,” the statement added. item.description: Architect Shettima Muhammad Kashim, son of the late Sir Kashim Ibrahim, the first indigenous governor of the defunct Northern Region, has died in a road accident in Abuja. Shettima, 67, reportedly died on Friday, October 16, hours after attending a book launch examining President Bola Tinubu’s administration. His remains were buried at Gudu Cemetery, Abuja on Saturday in accordance with Islamic rites after funeral prayers held at the National Mosque attended by dozens, including Vice President Kashim Shettima. Friends who were with him at the book launch described him as a humble, jovial and dependable person who maintained cordial relationships across political divides despite his family’s prominent place in Nigeria’s political history. Among those who paid tribute to him were Dr Garba Abari, former Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), and Professor Usman Yusuf, former Executive Secretary of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS). Abari said he spent several hours with the deceased on Friday before leaving for the Juma’at prayer, unaware that their meeting would be their last. “We were together with him, one other very close friend of his, Professor Usman Yusuf, and yet another friend of ours, Comrade Kalli Gazali,” Abari said. Abari said he left the group for the Friday prayer at Banex Mosque, while Kashim and the others proceeded to Maitama Juma’at Mosque, popularly known as Yar’Adua Mosque. According to him, Kashim later took his friends home after the prayers and lunch before driving towards his residence in Asokoro, where the fatal accident occurred. Abari said the news of Kashim’s death was particularly shocking because the deceased was known to be an extremely careful driver. “One thing that is distinctive about him is that he is an extremely careful, cautious driver,” Abari said, adding that the same caution characterised the way Kashim approached his responsibilities. Describing him as a person who never flaunted his privileged family background, Abari said Kashim was well brought up, good-natured and friendly to people regardless of their social standing. “He was a personification of humility, never carrying any airs around him about the kind of family he came from,” he said. Abari added that although Kashim came from a political family and held his own political views, he never allowed political differences to damage his relationships with others. The former NOA director-general said the suddenness of the death was a reminder of the uncertainty of human life. “If I recall the moments we had together, I recall the banters, everything. He looked too far away from death. But we never knew that it was just hovering around,” he said. He prayed that Allah would forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. ‘We were friends for almost 50 years’ Yusuf, who said he had known Kashim for almost five decades, described him as a decent, dependable and God-fearing person. In his tribute, the former NHIS executive secretary said their friendship began at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and endured for nearly 50 years. “Arch. Shettima Mohammed Kashim and I met in ABU Zaria and have been very good friends for almost 50 years,” he said. Recounting their final hours together, Yusuf said they attended the book launch at the Yar’Adua Centre on Friday and left the venue at about 1:20pm. He said they proceeded to a mosque in Wuse II for the Friday prayer before having lunch at a nearby restaurant. They later observed the Asr prayer at the mosque before Kashim dropped him at his residence at about 4:30pm. Yusuf said he received a call from Kashim’s son about half an hour later, informing him that the family had been told that his father’s car was involved in an accident in Asokoro and that the occupant had been taken to Asokoro General Hospital. He said he rushed to the hospital, where he met members of Kashim’s family and brothers, who informed him that the architect had died. According to Yusuf, Kashim’s car ran into a stationary truck, resulting in fatal injuries. “Shettima Mohammed Kashim was more than a friend to me and many. He was a good, decent, dependable and God-fearing person,” he said. “May Allah forgive all his shortcomings and reward him with Jannatul Firdaus,” he prayed. He said the deceased was trained as an architect and remained committed to his profession rather than using his family connections to pursue a political career. Abari recalled that Kashim served as general manager of the Borno Housing Corporation in the 1980s before moving to the federal service, where he also worked with the Federal Housing Authority. His career, Abari said, reflected a commitment to the profession in which he was trained. “He did not abandon his training as an architect,” he said. Kashim was also known by the traditional title of Shettima of Borno, a title associated with his family’s longstanding place in the traditional and political history of the region. Yusuf said the title had a historical connection to his father, Sir Kashim Ibrahim, who was conferred with the title of Shettima of Borno in 1935 and later became Waziri of Borno in 1956. Sir Kashim Ibrahim served as the first indigenous governor of the Northern Region of Nigeria from 1962 to 1966. Although his father occupied a prominent position in the country’s political history, Abari said Kashim remained approachable and maintained friendships with people of different backgrounds and political persuasions. Kashim was married to a daughter of the late Alhaji Mai Deribe, a renowned businessman.

item.title: ADAMAWA FOR ASIWAJU!
item.description: The Microphone Has Been Tested. The Signal Is Strong. The Structure Is Ready. Adamawa is ready, and its message is clear: the political structure, leadership and grassroots network are firmly in place to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and all All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates in the 2027 general elections. With Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri providing leadership, direction and strategic coordination, the state is prepared to pursue a decisive victory. The commitment is firm, the objective is clear, and the target is 100% electoral victory across the board. Achieving this goal requires sustained engagement, unity of purpose and disciplined organisation. Every stakeholder, coordinator and supporter has a role to play in taking the message to the people and translating commitment into votes. At the centre of this mobilisation is the Adamawa Renewed Hope 226 Movement (ARH-226M), led by its Director-General, Professor Abdullahi Liman Tukur. It is a structured, coordinated, knowledge-driven and grassroots-focused political movement established to transform political support into organised electoral action. Its reach extends across every level of the state’s political landscape: * 4,104 Polling Units: Where every vote counts and community engagement must translate into electoral participation. * 226 Electoral Wards: Where grassroots mobilisation takes shape, relationships are strengthened and local priorities receive attention. * 21 Local Government Areas: Where leadership, coordination and stakeholder engagement connect the statewide mission with community action. Through its 21 experienced LGA coordinators, clear leadership structures and effective mobilisation strategies, ARH-226M is prepared to reach communities, engage stakeholders and consolidate support for the APC from the polling units to the state level. The task is to sustain a visible presence, listen to the people, communicate the Renewed Hope message clearly and encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and confidently in the electoral process. From community meetings to stakeholder consultations, every engagement must strengthen trust, widen participation and reinforce a shared commitment to victory. With consistent follow-through and cooperation across party structures, the movement can keep its mobilisation focused and responsive to local realities. This coordinated effort will turn readiness into action, action into mobilisation and mobilisation into victory. Adamawa is ready. The structure is in place. The mission is achievable. One State. One Purpose. A Shared Commitment to Renewed Hope. With Fintiri as the leader, Adamawa will deliver, Insha Allah!
